title.narrative: provision of integrated, life-saving Nutrition assistance to the most severely affected communities in Tayeeglow District, Bakool Region.

description.narrative: ltpgtCRPD will implement a 9-month nutrition project across five villages of Biyooley, Koorar, El-Garas village, Shimo and Tiyeglow/Sinai in Tayeeglow District to reduce malnutrition among children under five and pregnant and lactating women (PLWs). The project will target 10,440 direct individuals (3,200 Women, 3,200 Girls, 3,400 Boys and 640 men). The project will align with Somalia’s IMAM and MIYCAN guidelines and will be delivered in close coordination with the SWS MoH, community leaders and Area-Based Coordination groups. Standardized Nutrition Cluster monitoring and evaluation tools will be applied to ensure quality, consistency, and accountability. Throughout the project, targeted mapping and inclusive strategies will actively engage marginalized and minority groups, ensuring their meaningful participation and representation. Data will be disaggregated by age, gender, disability, and minority status to monitor inclusion and outcomes. Recruitment will prioritize minority staff to reflect community diversity and enhance program relevance.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtCHWs will be trained to conduct routine household-level nutrition screening for children under five and PLWs. This will be supplemented by Family MUAC screening led by caregivers and mass MUAC and oedema screening campaigns. CHWs will refer children with moderate acute malnutrition (MAM) to TSFP and severe acute malnutrition (SAM) cases to OTPs or stabilization centers managed by partners. Eligibility of beneficiaries will be decided through transparent, community-led processes. Beneficiaries must participate in IYCF education sessions and cooking demonstrations to reinforce behavior change. A comprehensive CFM will be implemented to collect around 280 entries through feedback desks, suggestion boxes, and verbal reports to CHWs and MTMSG members. Community sensitization activities using Somali-language materials will increase awareness on safe reporting related to PSEA, PDAD, GBV, and child protection. Five referral pathways—one per village—will link community members to health, protection, legal, and psychosocial services. Community-based protection committees will strengthen the capacity to identify and respond to protection risks, reinforce complaints mechanisms, and prioritize inclusion of women, persons with disabilities, youth, and minority clans.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe main activities include:lt/pgtltpgtltbrgt1. Train CHWs in screening, identification, and referral of acutely malnourished children, pregnant, and breastfeeding women.ltbrgt2. Admit children with SAM and medical complications to SCs for intensive treatmentltbrgt4. Refer children with SAM to OTPs for therapeutic care.ltbrgt5. Implement door-to-door visits by CHWs to identify and refer malnourished children and pregnant and breastfeeding women.ltbrgt6. Conduct group IYCF education sessions at the health facilities/ nutrition sitesltbrgt7. Implement door-to-door visits by CHWs to identify and refer malnourished children and pregnant and breastfeeding women.ltbrgt8. Analyze and improve recovery rates for pregnant and breastfeeding women.ltbrgt9. Support establishment of demonstration gardens at the facility/community level to promote dietary diversity among children less than 2 years.ltbrgt10. Train nutrition workers on Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP).ltbrgt12. Facilitate community feedback sessions to improve accountability to affected populations.ltbrgt13. Conduct nutrition surveys incorporating GBV, AAP, PSEA, and CP indicators.ltbrgt14. Monitor and report cure rates among children treated in OTPs.ltbrgtlt/pgt
